source.author: lucr
source.text: tum porro puer, ut saevis proiectus ab undis navita, nudus humi iacet infans indigus omni vitali auxilio, cum primum in luminis oras nixibus ex alvo matris natura profudit, vagituque locum lugubri complet, ut aequumst cui tantum in vita restet transire malorum.
source.text_original: tum porro puer, ut saevis proiectus ab undis / navita, nudus humi iacet infans indigus omni / vitali auxilio, cum primum in luminis oras / nixibus ex alvo matris natura profudit, / vagituque locum lugubri complet, ut aequumst / cui tantum in vita restet transire malorum.
source.text_english: Then further, the child, like a sailor cast out by savage waves, lies naked on the ground, a helpless infant in need of every aid to life, when nature first has poured him forth from his mother’s womb onto the shores of light, and fills the place with mournful crying, as is fitting for one who has so much evil left to pass through in life.

reuse.author: lact
reuse.text: itaque naturam non matrem esse humani generis, sed nouercam, quae cum mutis tam liberaliter gesserit, hominem uero sic effuderit, ut inops et infirmus et omni auxilio indigens nihil aliud possit quam fragilitatis suae condicionem ploratu ac ominari, scilicet cui tantum in uita restet transire malorum.
reuse.text_original: itaque naturam non matrem esse humani generis, sed nouercam, quae cum mutis tam liberaliter gesserit, hominem uero sic effuderit, ut inops et infirmus et omni auxilio indigens nihil aliud possit quam fragilitatis suae condicionem ploratu ac ominari, scilicet cui tantum in uita restet transire malorum.
reuse.text_english: Therefore nature is not the mother of the human race but a stepmother, who, though she has dealt so generously with the dumb creatures, has brought forth man in such a way that, helpless and weak and in need of every aid, he can do nothing except lament and bemoan the condition of his frailty, since there is left to him in life only to pass through a multitude of evils.
